findings.failure: Cancel/error exits do not prove ledger release per kind. Cancelled returns before any acquisition; the stored 'error exit' is RetargetedDescriptor, refused before acquisition; (0,0,0) is asserted only after owner.release_population(), so an implementation that leaks a consumer lease until generation retirement passes. No stored kind has a port/build-failure or mid-consumption cancel.
findings.required_enforcement: Per stored kind: acquire, then cancel/drop and fail during build (injected DerivedPort error) and assert required bytes 0 before release_population; keep the post-retirement (0,0,0) check.

findings.failure: The 21-field privacy probe passes if any field stays private: the runner only requires every emitted error to be E0616, not one per field. Making CacheBackend.graphs pub(crate) leaves 20 matching errors and the probe passes. A new field is never accessed by the probe, contradicting its comment.
findings.required_enforcement: One refuse probe per field (or assert error count == field count), and an exhaustive destructure `let CacheBackend { f1, .., f21 } = cache;` without `..` in the owner accept probe so a new field fails to compile.

findings.failure: The shared Canonical-authored rule was edited in place at an already-placed version (0.1.0, also locked by asymptote and tastemaker) to add a ryo product path exemption inside its query, contradicting its own 'No exception or baseline is supplied'. The new scenarios were never validated: tm_guards validates only ryo-local assets, not no-heap-accounting.
findings.required_enforcement: Revert 0.1.0; scope the ledger through ryo's tastemaker.toml placement exclude (or publish a new rule version with a generic owner parameter); run tm validate on the asset and record it.

findings.failure: Direct builder bypass is not impossible: DerivedPort exposes DerivedUseCase::build publicly, and any file_dag holder of Arc<dyn DerivedPort> can call port.build(..) outside derived/owner, skipping admission, ledger and lease. Only call sites in owner/acquisition/semantics/service.rs do so today; nothing prevents a new one.
findings.required_enforcement: Hold the port only inside DerivedOwner (owner-private newtype) or a TM rule restricting DerivedUseCase::build calls to derived/owner/acquisition/semantics, with bad/good scenarios and a compile-fail probe.

findings.failure: An unenumerated derived consumer outside the owner: cached_graph.rs (file_dag) drives acquire_graph/acquire_graph_domain/DemandAnswers with Option<&mut CacheBackend>; None or graph_enabled!=Enabled silently declines to 'the existing ordinary traversal', a second route chosen by cache presence. CacheBackend itself is RefCell<Option<..>> in DerivedOwner (owner.rs:101).
findings.required_enforcement: Move CachedGraph into derived/owner (or make the backend non-optional per prepared file and pass &mut), list it in the ryo-brdm consumer census with a control for the decline route, and a probe that a non-owner cannot pass None.
